stories.headline: US strikes Iran for 9th night as American death toll hits 17; Iran hits Gulf allies, missiles near Israel

key_facts.fact: US Central Command launched a new round of airstrikes early Monday, its ninth straight night, targeting Iranian military command centers, air defense and coastal surveillance sites, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites and communications networks.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military's Central Command announced a new round of strikes early Monday, now into their ninth straight night. Central Command said it targeted 'Iranian military command centers, air defense and coastal surveillance sites, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites and communications networks.'

key_facts.fact: The US military death toll in the conflict rose to 17 after a service member was killed Saturday in Iraq during a controlled detonation of a downed Iranian drone, a day after two others were killed in an Iranian attack on a base in Jordan; more than 430 US troops have been wounded.
key_facts.excerpt: An American service member was killed Saturday in Iraq during 'controlled detonation' of a downed Iranian drone... Sunday's announcement brings the death toll of U.S. service members to 17 during the conflict with Iran. More than 430 American troops have been wounded.

key_facts.fact: Iran fired drones and missiles at Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan on Sunday; Kuwait reported a fire at a power and water plant, and Iran's army said it targeted a US ammunition depot at Camp al-Adiri and air defense radars at the Ali Al Salem airbase in Kuwait.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has fired drones and missiles at Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan... the Iranian army said it targeted a US ammunition depot at Camp al-Adiri and air defence radars at the Ali Al Salem airbase, which hosts US personnel.

key_facts.fact: Iran launched four missiles toward the Jordanian port city of Aqaba, and Israel's military said projectiles could spill over, warning Israelis to expect their first air-raid sirens in weeks; interceptors were launched near Eilat against falling debris.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel's military said Iranian missiles launched toward the Jordanian port city of Aqaba just across the border could spill over, warning Israelis to expect the first air-raid sirens in weeks.

key_facts.fact: Iranian authorities said at least 50 people have been killed and 517 wounded in US strikes over the past three weeks; recent US strikes have hit bridges, water desalination plants and electrical facilities in Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian authorities on Sunday said at least 50 people have been killed and 517 wounded in the latest U.S. strikes.

key_facts.fact: President Trump said the new strikes were carried out in honor of the killed troops: 'we hit them very hard again tonight, and we did that in honor of' the fallen service members.
key_facts.excerpt: 'So we'll see what happens. But we hit them very hard again tonight, and we did that in honor of the probably three,' the president added.

key_facts.fact: The full-scale war with Iran resumed on July 7 after a June interim ceasefire collapsed; both sides have struck critical infrastructure, Tehran has declared the Strait of Hormuz closed, and Washington has reimposed a blockade of Iranian ports.
key_facts.excerpt: Washington has reimposed its blockade of Iranian ports and Tehran has declared the Strait of Hormuz closed and targeted US allies in the region, as a preliminary ceasefire collapsed less than a month after it began.

stories.headline: Brent crude tops $90 for first time since June as Hormuz shipping stalls; US gasoline nears $4

key_facts.fact: Brent crude reached $90.75 per barrel on July 19, a roughly 3% single-session gain and a five-week high, while West Texas Intermediate rose about 2.5% to settle near $83.85, as Strait of Hormuz vessel traffic collapsed amid US-Iran fighting.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude reached $90.75 per barrel by 19:51 ET on 19 July 2026, marking a gain of approximately 3% on the session and a five-week high. West Texas Intermediate advanced around 2.5% over the same period, settling at $83.85 per barrel.

key_facts.fact: It was Brent's first move above $90 a barrel since mid-June, building on last week's gains after the US-Iran ceasefire deteriorated and tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slowed.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude's move above $90 a barrel — its first since mid-June — builds on last week's gains after the U.S.-Iran ceasefire deteriorated further, reducing tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: The nationwide average US gasoline price was just below the politically important $4-per-gallon mark on Sunday and was likely to rise above that level Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: The nationwide average U.S. gasoline price was just below the politically important $4-per-gallon mark Sunday, per AAA, and is likely to rise above that level Monday.

key_facts.fact: Brent and WTI rose nearly 16% last week while the S&P 500 fell 1.55%, putting Wall Street on notice for oil-driven inflation.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent and WTI crude rose nearly 16% last week, while the S&P 500 fell 1.55%.

key_facts.fact: Futures put roughly a 15% probability on the Fed raising rates in July, rising to about 65% by September; June consumer prices dropped 0.4% and annual inflation eased to 3.5%, aided by a 9.7% fall in gasoline prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Futures indicate a roughly 15% probability of the Fed raising rates in July. The likelihood increases to about 65% by September... Consumer prices in June dropped by 0.4%, with annual inflation easing to 3.5%. A significant factor was a 9.7% drop in gasoline prices.

key_facts.fact: Analysts warn supply buffers are thin, with the roughly 400 million barrels of excess inventories at the start of the war largely depleted.
key_facts.excerpt: A recent FT report cited Energy Aspect's Amrita Sen, who warned that the roughly 400 million barrels of excess inventories at the start of the war have largely been depleted.

stories.headline: Russia launches largest ballistic missile barrage on Kyiv of the war; 20 killed across Ukraine

key_facts.fact: Overnight on July 19, Russia attacked Ukraine with 41 missiles and 125 attack drones, including 25 Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles and 10 Zircon hypersonic missiles, with Kyiv the primary target.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia launched 41 missiles and 125 attack drones across Ukraine overnight, according to the Ukrainian air force. The attack included 25 ballistic missiles.

key_facts.fact: Acting Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the barrage was the largest ballistic missile attack on Kyiv since the war began in February 2022; President Zelensky called it one of Russia's 'largest ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv.'
key_facts.excerpt: Acting Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the missile barrage targeting Kyiv was the largest since the war began in February 2022.

key_facts.fact: The Kyiv strikes killed at least one person and injured around 15-17, sparking fires and structural damage across five districts and damaging the Lukianivska metro station.
key_facts.excerpt: The strikes killed one person and injured 17 within the city, causing fires and structural damage in the Desnianskyi, Dniprovskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, Sviatoshynskyi, and Solomianskyi districts. The Lukianivska metro station was damaged and temporarily closed.

key_facts.fact: Russian attacks killed 20 people and injured at least 142 across Ukraine over the day; a midday missile strike on postal giant Nova Poshta's terminal in the suburbs of Kharkiv killed at least four people.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian attacks killed 20 people and injured at least 142 others across Ukraine over the past day... a Russian missile strike hit Ukrainian postal giant Nova Poshta's terminal in the suburbs of the country's second-largest city, Kharkiv... The mid-day attack killed at least four people.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's air defenses intercepted or suppressed 126 of 166 targets, downing 17 of 25 ballistic missiles, a sharp improvement from an earlier July attack when it intercepted none, indicating replenished Patriot interceptor stocks.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine said it shot down at least 17 ballistic missiles in Sunday's attack, indicating it may have replenished some of its dwindling stockpile of Patriot interceptor missiles. During a major Russian attack earlier this month, Ukraine was unable to intercept any ballistic missiles.

stories.headline: EU fines AliExpress €550M, its largest-ever DSA penalty, over illegal-product sales

key_facts.fact: The European Commission on Monday fined Chinese online marketplace AliExpress €550 million ($629 million) for failing to adequately crack down on the sale of unsafe and counterfeit products under the Digital Services Act.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission on Monday fined Chinese online marketplace AliExpress 550 million euros ($629 million) for failing to adequately crack down on the sale of unsafe and counterfeit products on its site.

key_facts.fact: The penalty is the biggest ever imposed for breaches of the EU's Digital Services Act, following a €200 million fine on rival retailer Temu and a €120 million penalty on Elon Musk's X.
key_facts.excerpt: The fine, the biggest ever imposed for breaches of the 27-nation European Union's Digital Services Act, comes just months after another online retailer, Temu, was fined 200 million euros for similar breaches. Last year, Brussels issued a $120 million penalty for Elon Musk's social media site X.

key_facts.fact: The Commission, which opened its investigation in March 2024, found AliExpress overestimated the effectiveness of its detection system, that illegal products often stayed online for weeks and reappeared, and that its brand-authorization system was ineffective and understaffed.
key_facts.excerpt: The EU said AliExpress' 'overestimated the effectiveness of its system in detecting and removing illegal products'. Millions of products would also reappear... The platform also did not 'adequately' stop the sale of counterfeit products because its mandatory 'brand authorisation' system 'proved ineffective and understaffed.'

key_facts.fact: AliExpress, a subsidiary of Alibaba, must pay the fine and submit an action plan by October 20 to remedy the breach or risk periodic penalty payments.
key_facts.excerpt: The commission said that AliExpress now has until Oct. 20 to submit an action plan setting out measures to 'remedy the breach of its obligations to assess and mitigate systemic risks.'

key_facts.fact: Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen said the spread of counterfeit clothing, unsafe toys and dangerous cosmetics 'is not an unavoidable cost of shopping online — it is a failure by AliExpress to comply with its obligations under the Digital Services Act.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The spread of counterfeit clothing, unsafe toys, dangerous cosmetics and other illegal and harmful products is not an unavoidable cost of shopping online — it is a failure by AliExpress to comply with its obligations under the Digital Services Act,' Henna Virkkunen... said in a statement.

stories.headline: Samsung Biologics to buy Switzerland's PolyPeptide for $1.8B in Korea's biggest biopharma M&A

key_facts.fact: Samsung Biologics said on Monday it had made an all-cash bid of 1.46 billion Swiss francs (about $1.8 billion) for Switzerland's PolyPeptide Group, a specialist in peptide-based active pharmaceutical ingredients.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea's Samsung Biologics said on Monday that it had made an all-cash bid of 1.46 billion Swiss francs ($1.8 billion) for Switzerland's PolyPeptide Group, which specializes in peptide-based active pharmaceutical ingredients.

key_facts.fact: The deal, valued at roughly 2.7 trillion won, is the largest merger and acquisition in the history of Korea's pharmaceutical and biotech industry.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Biologics has agreed to acquire a leading global peptide contract development and manufacturing organization in a deal worth approximately 2.7 trillion won ($1.81 billion)... the largest merger and acquisition in the history of Korea's pharmaceutical and biotech industry.

key_facts.fact: Under the public tender offer, shareholders will receive 44.31 Swiss francs per share, and the transaction is expected to close by the end of the year, with Samsung aiming to expand into peptide therapeutics to tap the booming weight-loss drug market.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the terms of the public tender offer, stockholders will receive 44.31 Swiss franc per share. The transaction is expected to close by the end of this year... the company will expand its pipeline into peptide therapeutics to tap into the booming weight-loss drug market.

key_facts.fact: Draupnir Holding, PolyPeptide's largest shareholder with a 55.65% stake, has committed to tendering its entire holding, but the offer requires more than 66.7% of all outstanding shares to be tendered to succeed.
key_facts.excerpt: Draupnir Holding B.V., the largest shareholder, has committed to tendering its entire 55.65% stake in the offer. However, for the tender offer to succeed, more than 66.7% of all outstanding shares must be tendered.

key_facts.fact: The acquisition broadens Samsung Biologics' contract-manufacturing business beyond antibody drugs and antibody-drug conjugates, driven by surging demand for peptide-based GLP-1 therapies for obesity and diabetes.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Biologics said that the acquisition will broaden... scope of its existing offerings centered on antibody drugs and antibody-drug conjugates... driven by peptide-based GLP-1 therapies for obesity and diabetes.

stories.headline: Wildfire north of Madrid burns 13,000 hectares as Spain battles multiple summer blazes

key_facts.fact: A wildfire that started Thursday in Guadalajara province north of Madrid had burned more than 13,000 hectares (32,000 acres) by Sunday and forced some 700 residents to evacuate, authorities said.
key_facts.excerpt: Firefighters were battling a wildfire north of Madrid on Sunday that has burned around 13,000 hectares (32,000 acres) of land and forced some 700 residents to evacuate, authorities said.

key_facts.fact: More than 500 firefighters and 25 firefighting aircraft were deployed as the flames advanced a further 14 kilometers overnight.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 500 firefighters and emergency personnel have been deployed to contain the blaze. Ground crews are also being assisted by 25 firefighting aircraft, officials said... the flames had advanced a further 14 kilometers (9 miles) overnight.

key_facts.fact: A separate blaze near Zaragoza in northeastern Spain had burned nearly 16,000 hectares since Wednesday and was described as 'far from under control.'
key_facts.excerpt: It comes hot on the heels of a blaze that started on Wednesday near Zaragoza, in the northeast, has burned nearly 16,000 hectares and is 'far from under control.'

key_facts.fact: Earlier this month, one of Spain's deadliest wildfires in recent history killed 13 people and destroyed 7,000 hectares in the southern province of Almeria.
key_facts.excerpt: The country is still reeling from one of the deadliest wildfires in modern times that killed 13 people and destroyed 7,000 hectares in southern Almeria province earlier this month.

key_facts.fact: Since the start of the year, wildfires have destroyed more than 80,000 hectares across Spain, nearly double the area burned during the same period last year; scientists link the trend to human-caused climate change intensifying heatwaves.
key_facts.excerpt: Since the beginning of the year, wildfires have destroyed more than 80,000 hectares across Spain, nearly double the area burned during the same period last year. Scientists say human-caused climate change is making heatwaves longer, hotter and more frequent.

stories.headline: Flash floods and landslides kill at least 12 in India's Jammu and Kashmir; several missing

key_facts.fact: At least 12 people were killed and several others, including a Jal Shakti Department employee, remain missing after torrential rain triggered flash floods and landslides in the Poonch and Rajouri border districts of Jammu and Kashmir on Sunday, July 19.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 12 persons were killed in separate rain-related incidents in the two districts on Sunday (July 19, 2026), while the fate of seven people missing, including an employee of the Jal Shakti Department, remains unknown.

key_facts.fact: The worst devastation hit the Lower Murrah area of Surankote tehsil in Poonch, where floodwaters and landslide debris buried homes; officials said eight members of one family were swept away.
key_facts.excerpt: Officials said Lower Murrah in Surankote suffered the heaviest loss, where eight members of a family were swept away.

key_facts.fact: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah cut short a New Delhi visit to oversee relief operations and announced ex gratia relief of 6 lakh rupees for the next of kin of each person killed.
key_facts.excerpt: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Monday (July 20, 2026) announced an ex gratia relief of ₹6 lakh for the next of kin of those killed in rain-related incidents in Rajouri and Poonch districts.

key_facts.fact: The Amarnath Yatra and pilgrimages to Vaishno Devi and Shiv Khori were temporarily suspended, and traffic on the strategic Jammu-Srinagar NH-44 was disrupted, after the weather service forecast adverse conditions.
key_facts.excerpt: Annual Amarnath Yatra, which began July 3, and pilgrimages to Vaishno Devi shrine in Katra and Shiv Khori in Reasi were temporarily suspended after IMD forecast adverse weather for the next three days.

key_facts.fact: The Meteorological Department warned of an extended wet spell with flash floods, landslides and mudslides across vulnerable areas of Jammu and Kashmir from July 19 to July 23.
key_facts.excerpt: The Meteorological Department Kashmir has warned of flash floods, landslides, mudslides and shooting stones in vulnerable areas of Jammu and Kashmir due to extended wet spell from July 19 to July 23.
